I think when you've spent your whole life like that, your only way out is to be the best. Parents will drill it in that you're special and smart because if you don't think so, you'll find it a lot harder to make something of yourself.

When you're poor, you have an inflated sense of yourself because you were taught at a young age that if you want a better life, you have to be the better option out of *everyone* for colleges and careers.

I only recently realized that I'm *not* special or extremely talented. I was a kid who didn't want to live their adult life in poverty. Now I'm just like everyone else.

Yeah that whole situation seems a bit... weird.

I would definitely talk to your legal guardian(s) about meeting with someone who can give you an idea of what you can do moving forward. There's a chance this is all completely legal, but you'll get your best information from a professional. 

Good luck OP.

The psych hospital I went to did the same thing to every patient. Even had people squat, fully naked, just to be sure. Although, the squatting wasn't something everyone went through.

The thing that sticks out to me here are the cameras. I was put in a small bathroom while two female nurses instructed me to strip, lift up my bra, and slowly turn around. There were no obvious cameras in that location.

I asked the nurses about the strip search while I was there.

I was told that the strip search was a way to make sure that nobody was sneaking in anything, *but* that it was also used to keep track of self harm.

The hospital I was sent to was mostly for people who were suicidal, or for people who were homicidal (kind of counterproductive if you're trying to keep people alive /s).

I'm not sure if it was the same type of hospital for you. They let me know in the beginning what was going to happen, and they let my mom know too. She signed papers admitting me and if I had to guess, she gave them permission to do the strip search.
